title: Chiral eating flocks, negative: rotating the polarization bounds the fronts of the Toner-Tu eaters, but gives either churning crescent fragments (chi 0.03-0.08) or still, splitting spots (chi >= 0.1), never persistent motile individuals
summary: Follow-up to 20261027T0210-c51-toner-tu-eaters-fronts: adding a chiral rotation chi of the polarization (dp += chi p x z) to the eating Toner-Tu flocks curls the fronts that otherwise align into box-spanning bands. At chi 0.01 fronts persist; at chi 0.03 the population becomes discrete crescent hooks with dim wakes (chi03_strip.png), but they churn: at 10 t per frame the longest track is 30 frames (300 t), 788 nucleations, merge/split 0.73, 0 persistent splits, 5 tracks move >= 1 body length. chi 0.06 and 0.08: longest track 13 and 133 frames, merge/split 0.82 and 0.97, 0 persistent splits. chi 0.1 and 0.2: round spots that rotate in place and split like Gray-Scott spots (9 and 46 persistent tracks, 4 and 22 persistent splits, generation 2-3) but move less than one body length.

finding.operator: chiral rotation of the polarization in Toner-Tu flocks growing on a consumed food
finding.control: chirality scan chi 0, 0.01, 0.03, 0.06, 0.08, 0.1, 0.2 at fixed kinetics (seed 0; chi 0.03 also seed 1)
finding.result: chi 0.03: longest track 300 t, 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.73; chi 0.06/0.08: 0 persistent splits, merge/split 0.82/0.97; chi 0.1/0.2: 4/22 persistent splits, gen 2/3, max 0.8 body lengths moved

limits: Seed 0 only for most of the scan, one grid and step, kinetics fixed at the Gray-Scott spot point of the parent. The crescents at chi 0.03 look like individuals in single frames (h_all.png row 2) but are excitable wave fragments that re-ignite from wakes; labkit's threshold choice changes the counts but not the churn (0.36 and 0.59 of range both give 0 persistent splits). The class still lacks a bounded motile body; a conserved agent number (no growth) or a long-range self-repellent are the untried routes.
